subject: physics
question_text: Define the specific heat capacity of a substance. On what factors does it depend?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 Very Short Answer Question 6 (printed p.124). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The two-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: S = (1/m)(dQ/dT) is heat per unit mass per degree, SI unit J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and it depends on the nature of the substance and the temperature at which it is measured — this is the per-unit-mass definition, distinct from the molar specific heat capacity of vsaq8, which the relation C_P − C_V = R of vsaq9 belongs to, never this one directly.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. The definition, S = (1/m)(dQ/dT), and its SI unit.
steps.why: Writing S as heat per unit mass per degree keeps it different from the molar specific heat capacity, which is measured per mole.
common_mistakes: Leaving out unit mass — without it the definition is heat capacity, not specific heat capacity.
Giving the unit as J kg⁻¹ only, without the K⁻¹ for the degree.

recall.must_convey: That specific heat capacity is the heat needed to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance through one degree, S equals one over m times dQ by dT, SI unit joule per kilogram per kelvin.
accept: heat per unit mass per degree
S equals one by m dQ by dT

steps.memory_tip: Specific means per unit mass — S is heat per kilogram per kelvin.

lines: It depends on the nature of the
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name both factors — the substance and its temperature.
steps.why: The same substance has a different specific heat capacity at different temperatures, so temperature is a real second factor, not a detail of the measurement.
common_mistakes: Naming only the substance and leaving out temperature.
Naming mass as a factor — S is defined PER unit mass, so mass itself does not change its value.

recall.must_convey: That specific heat capacity depends on the nature of the substance and on the temperature at which it is measured.

steps.memory_tip: Two factors: what it is made of, and how hot it already is.

insider_note: S is defined per unit MASS — contrast with the molar specific heat capacity, which is measured per mole. Keep the two straight.
